newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican authorities take aim at deadly drug cartel.
newsitem.headline: Mexican authorities take aim at deadly drug cartel.

text.p: Mexican authorities searched the homes of two suspected hitmen for Mexico's most feared drug cartel but turned up only one AK-47 assault rifle, the official news agency Notimex reported on Sunday.
Citing authorities from the Attorney General's Office, Notimex said a judge gave federal agents a search warrant to enter the two homes in Tijuana, on the U.S. border across from San Diego.

Tijuana is the home base of the Arellano Felix brothers, who run a cocaine smuggling ring that U.S. anti-drug authorities have called the most cut-throat in Mexico. The Mexican government has placed a $1 million bounty on their heads.
The two were identified as Fabian Martinez Gonzalez, or "Shark," and Eduardo Leon, Notimex said. They were suspected of murdering several federal law-enforcement officials.
Police found the AK-47 rifle in one of their homes, Notimex said, adding that federal authorities would continue their search for the two men.
The deaths this year of seven federal law-enforcement officers from Tijuana and other state and local officials have been widely blamed on drug cartels like that of the Arellano Felix brothers.
